name: Guiñote
description: Guiñote is a Tute variant for 2 to 4 players from Aragón, Navarra and Castilla. It uses the same 40-card Spanish deck and point-trick structure as Tute, but the jack and horse swap rank and point values; singing (cantes) uses king and jack; multiple 20s or 40s may be sung after a trick; and the winner of the last trick deals next.

content.text: Guiñote is a Tute variant for 2 to 4 players from Aragón, Navarra and Castilla. It uses the same 40-card Spanish deck and point-trick structure as Tute, but the jack and horse swap rank and point values; singing (cantes) uses king and jack; multiple 20s or 40s may be sung after a trick; and the winner of the last trick deals next.
Guiñote is a regional Tute variant played in Aragón, Navarra and part of Castilla. The name distinguishes it from standard Tute.

Standard Spanish 40-card pack: four suits (Oros, Copas, Espadas, Bastos), ranks Ace down to Two. In Guiñote the jack (sota) ranks above the horse (caballo) and is worth 3 points; the horse is worth 2. Same pack as Tute.
The first dealer is chosen at random. In Guiñote the winner of the last trick deals the next hand; if a hand ends by claim the winner of the game deals next.

items.text: Guiñote vs Tute: In Guiñote jack ranks above horse and is worth 3 points (horse 2); singing uses king and jack (not king and horse); multiple 20s or 40s may be sung after one trick; tute (four kings or four horses) is not valid; winner of last trick deals next.
